stories.headline: IDC: 80% of B2B Tech Buyers Now Use AI Agents in Purchasing — Both Sides of the Deal Are Automating Simultaneously
stories.summary: IDC research published in August 2026 confirms that eight in ten B2B technology buyers are already deploying AI agents as part of their procurement process — not a forecast, but current reality. A separate IDC report found that 45% of enterprise AI projects are failing to deliver results, with CIOs demanding clearer ROI and governance before scaling agentic workflows. For D&B, this is the sharpest validation yet of the AI Decision Intelligence thesis: agents on both the buy and sell side need verified, governed data as their foundation — exactly where D&B's entity resolution and commercial graph sit.

stories.headline: Apollo Acquires Pocus, Deepening Its Signal Intelligence Play Against ZoomInfo
stories.summary: Apollo confirmed on August 7, 2026 that it has acquired Pocus, an enterprise revenue intelligence platform used by Asana, Canva, and Monday.com, folding its AI-driven buying signal and workflow capabilities directly into Apollo's GTM stack. Pocus is no longer available as a standalone product, with its site redirecting to an Apollo waitlist. This move, alongside HubSpot's Warmly acquisition in June and Zoom's Common Room deal in July, signals that the GTM data consolidation wave is accelerating — platforms that own the system of record or engagement are hoovering up signal-layer companies, compressing the white space for pure-play data providers and raising the stakes for D&B's own embedding strategy.

stories.headline: Fiserv and Stuut Wire Agentic AI Into Enterprise Accounts Receivable, Targeting $2B+ B2B Invoice Backlog
stories.summary: Fiserv announced on August 5, 2026 a partnership with Stuut Technologies to embed agentic AI into enterprise order-to-cash, integrating its Commerce Hub and SnapPay platforms with Stuut's AI agent, which has already processed over $2 billion in B2B invoices. The deal targets the accounts receivable automation gap in large enterprise workflows, automating onboarding and invoice reconciliation end-to-end. This is a direct use case for D&B's Pipeline Risk & Revenue Protection and Account Intelligence agent archetypes — AR automation agents need entity resolution and payment behavior data (Paydex) to make creditworthy decisions at scale.

stories.headline: D&B Launches Agentic AI Capabilities for Compliance and Third-Party Risk, Cutting Processing Times by Up to 90%
stories.summary: Dun & Bradstreet announced in June 2026 new agentic capabilities embedded within its D&B Risk Analytics platform and accessible via its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, enabling organizations to cut compliance onboarding, screening, and due diligence processing times by 70–90%. The MCP server allows verified D&B data, models, and workflows to be embedded directly into AI assistants and custom agents across any platform. While not brand new, this story has fresh relevance this week as MCP adoption accelerates industry-wide — D&B's MCP server is a live embodiment of the 'be everywhere' neutrality strategy, positioning D&B as the trusted data layer inside third-party agentic stacks rather than competing to own the agent itself.

stories.headline: Big Tech's AI Debt Binge Is Distorting Credit Risk Metrics for Unrelated Safe-Haven Companies
stories.summary: Bloomberg reported on August 13, 2026 that a flood of debt issuance by US tech companies investing in AI infrastructure is inadvertently pushing up credit risk metrics — including credit default swap costs — for some of the world's safest non-tech firms, as competition for cash in the investment-grade market intensifies. BNP Paribas strategists attribute the contagion to AI-driven borrowing crowding out traditional safe-haven credit. For D&B, this illustrates why temporal analytics and real-time commercial risk signals matter more than ever — static credit scores are being distorted by macro AI investment flows, creating demand for dynamic, entity-level risk intelligence that can separate AI-exposure risk from underlying business fundamentals.

stories.headline: OpenAI S-1 Filing Imminent as Anthropic Posts First Profit — AI Lab IPO Race Accelerates
stories.summary: Anthropic recorded its first profit on August 13, 2026, while OpenAI's public S-1 prospectus is reported as imminent — two landmark financial milestones arriving simultaneously in what has been an IPO-watch year for frontier labs. This matters because it signals that the largest AI labs are crossing from capital-consumption phase into revenue-generation, shifting the investor narrative from growth bets to earnings multiples. For D&B, the commercialisation of frontier labs intensifies demand for the kind of explainable, auditable data signals — like Paydex and entity-resolved firmographics — that enterprise AI buyers require before embedding models into financial workflows.

stories.headline: xAI Ships Grok 4.6 Targeting Agentic Workloads — Matches GPT-5.6 on Intelligence Index
stories.summary: xAI released Grok 4.6 on August 12, 2026, explicitly optimised for long-running agents, coding, and multi-step knowledge work tasks, available immediately in Cursor, Grok Build, and via API with a 500K context window. The model matches GPT-5.6 Sol on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index composite benchmark, making it the first xAI model to reach direct parity with OpenAI at the frontier. This is a meaningful development for D&B's 'be everywhere' platform strategy: as xAI builds Grok deeper into agentic workflows and enterprise tooling, D&B's DUNS entity resolution and commercial data signals need to be available as a callable layer inside that ecosystem, not just Microsoft and Salesforce.

stories.headline: GPT-5.6 Luna Becomes ChatGPT Free Default After 80% Price Cut — Frontier AI Commodity Pricing Arrives
stories.summary: OpenAI slashed GPT-5.6 Luna pricing by 80% on July 30 — from $1 to $0.20 per million tokens — and on August 15 made it the default model for all free-tier ChatGPT users, putting frontier-grade AI in the hands of every consumer globally at effectively zero marginal cost. Google simultaneously crossed 1 billion monthly active Gemini users on August 11. The commoditisation of model access puts further pressure on raw AI capabilities as a moat and strengthens the case for proprietary data layers — precisely D&B's structural argument: when the model is free, the trusted ground truth data that makes agents accurate and defensible is where the value concentrates.

stories.headline: EU AI Act Transparency Rules Now Live — Chatbots, Deepfakes, and Synthetic Content Face Active Enforcement
stories.summary: From August 2, 2026, the European Commission's AI Office and national authorities began actively enforcing the EU AI Act's Article 50 transparency obligations: chatbots must disclose they are AI, deepfakes must be labelled, and AI-generated content must carry machine-readable marks. While high-risk system deadlines were previously deferred to December 2027 and August 2028 under the Digital Omnibus, this transparency enforcement layer is real and operative now, with penalties of up to €35 million or 7% of global revenue for non-compliance. For D&B, this accelerates enterprise demand for auditable, explainable AI outputs — the 'Explainability First / Ground Truth' pillar is no longer a nice-to-have but a legal hygiene requirement for any customer deploying AI in Europe.

stories.headline: Labour Regains Ground on Reform in Latest UK Polls as Political Landscape Stays Fragmented
stories.summary: New YouGov polling shows Labour has clawed back some support from Reform UK, though the broader electorate remains deeply fragmented across multiple parties. Reform continues to lead on immigration, with 35% of Britons rating them best on the issue, while Labour holds a narrow edge on NHS handling. The poll underscores how difficult the political terrain remains for Keir Starmer heading into the next election cycle.

stories.headline: US-Iran Peace Window Expires — Trump Threatens Oman Over Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The two-month Memorandum of Understanding between the US and Iran lapsed on Monday 17 August with no renewal in sight, as both sides traded accusations of violations. Iran's Foreign Minister said Tehran has not decided to restart negotiations, while mediators from Qatar and Pakistan continue shuttle diplomacy. Trump escalated tensions further by threatening to bomb Oman if it interferes with US operations in the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: James Webb Telescope Spots Star Near Galactic Centre Acting Like Nothing Seen Before
stories.summary: New observations from the James Webb Space Telescope of IRS 3, a star near the Milky Way's galactic centre, have produced results that are puzzling astronomers. Separately, Webb also captured striking new infrared images of NGC 2392 — the 'Lion Nebula' — revealing the dramatic final stages of a dying Sun-like star with a scorching white dwarf at its core. Both findings were published on 17 August 2026.

stories.headline: England's Jack Whaley Wins US Amateur at Merion Golf Club
stories.summary: Englishman Jack Whaley defeated Jay Leng Jr. in the championship match at Merion Golf Club to claim the 2026 US Amateur title. Whaley played through difficult conditions — including rain, double gloves and reportedly being stung by a wasp — to cap what Golf Channel described as a tremendous tournament. On the DP World Tour, the next event up is the Betfred British Masters hosted by Sir Nick Faldo at The Belfry, scheduled for 27–30 August.

stories.headline: Premier League Transfer Window Enters Final Fortnight — Gordon to Barcelona, Spurs Active
stories.summary: With the summer transfer window closing on 1 September at 11pm UK time, clubs are accelerating their business ahead of the 2026-27 season kicking off on 22 August. Newcastle United have already sold Anthony Gordon to Barcelona in a headline deal, while Tottenham Hotspur have completed a couple of free-transfer signings. Arsenal enter the new campaign as defending champions with the transfer deadline adding urgency to any remaining squad gaps.

stories.headline: France Retain Six Nations Title in 48–46 Thriller Against England — Ramos Penalty Seals It
stories.summary: France secured back-to-back Six Nations titles in March 2026 with a last-gasp penalty from Thomas Ramos to edge England 48–46 in a dramatic finale. Louis Bielle-Biarrey took Player of the Tournament with nine tries across the competition, setting a new Six Nations record. Ireland claimed the Triple Crown, while the result left England empty-handed despite pushing the champions to the final kick.

stories.headline: CERN Physicists Find Evidence of Gluon Saturation Inside Atomic Nuclei — A Physics First
stories.summary: Scientists at CERN have reported the first experimental evidence for gluon saturation inside atomic nuclei, a long-theorised state where gluons — the particles that bind quarks together — become so densely packed they start to overlap and interact with each other. The finding, published on 12 August, could reshape understanding of the strong nuclear force and the internal structure of protons and neutrons. It marks one of the most significant particle physics results in years.

stories.headline: The CapEx Train Keeps Rolling: How Wall Street Is Re-Rating AI Spend After Big Tech Q2 Earnings
stories.summary: Ben Thompson's August 14 weekly synthesis draws together the divergent Wall Street reactions to Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, and Google's Q2 2026 earnings, arguing that the market is now distinguishing between hyperscalers with a clear monetisation path and those spending without visible near-term returns. Thompson flags that Amazon's $220 billion capex raise — driven by memory costs and Jassy's assertion that demand will outpace capacity through 2027 and into 2028 — represents the most credible demand-signal yet for sustained AI infrastructure buildout. The piece is a direct counter to bubble narratives: real enterprise demand, not hype, is pulling forward spend. For D&B, this validates the 'be everywhere' platform strategy — enterprises are locking into cloud and agentic infrastructure now, and proprietary data layers like DUNS and Paydex that embed at the inference layer will compound in value as capacity comes online.

stories.headline: New York and the Power of the Network: Why Distribution Beats Model Capability in Platform Races
stories.summary: Published in the same August 14 Stratechery weekly, Thompson uses the network-effects logic of New York City to argue that in platform races, distribution density — not technical superiority — determines long-run winners, with modern Hollywood as a cautionary example of a network that hit its limits. Applied to AI, the argument is that agents and platforms which embed deepest into existing workflows will win, regardless of which underlying model is best. This directly mirrors D&B's 'Visa analogy' positioning: neutrality and ubiquitous embedding across Copilot, Agentforce, Bedrock, and Gemini matters more than backing any single model winner. It also reinforces why entity resolution as a foundational data layer — present everywhere, owned by no one platform — is structurally defensible.

stories.headline: At AI-Fueled Market Party, Wall Street Eyes the Rates Punch Bowl
stories.summary: Bloomberg's August 16 market analysis reports that enthusiasm for Big Tech's massive AI investments is driving equity markets to record highs, but identifies rising interest rates as the primary structural risk to the rally — noting that AI-related capex is not expected to fully pay off for years, making tech valuations especially sensitive to Treasury yields. The piece documents that the four hyperscalers are now projected to spend nearly $700 billion combined in 2026, up sharply from 2025, with free cash flow turning negative at Amazon and approaching zero at Meta. For D&B, this is a critical signal on the M&A and valuation environment: if rates rise and the market reprices long-duration AI bets, acquirers will favour assets with near-term, explainable ROI — precisely what D&B's Paydex, Buydex, and entity-resolution products deliver as grounding infrastructure for agentic workflows rather than speculative model plays.

data_science.tagline: Replacing gut-feel decisions with causal evidence — at scale, in production.
data_science.what_it_is: A/B testing is the discipline of randomly assigning users, accounts, or model variants to two or more treatment conditions and measuring the causal effect of that change on a target metric. It is the gold standard for validating product, model, and go-to-market decisions because randomisation breaks confounding — you know the difference in outcomes is caused by the treatment, not by who happened to see it. Modern experimentation frameworks extend classical two-sample t-tests into sequential testing, multi-armed bandits, switchback designs for network effects, and CUPED variance reduction, making experiments faster and cheaper without inflating false-positive rates.
data_science.how_it_works:
1. HYPOTHESIS & UNIT OF RANDOMISATION — Define what you are changing (a model score threshold, a UI element, an email subject line) and the unit you randomise over (user, account, DUNS number, territory). The unit must be the same as the unit of interference — if accounts talk to each other (network effects), randomising by account can leak treatment into control.

2. SAMPLE SIZE & POWER CALCULATION — Before running, compute required N using: n = 2σ²(z_α + z_β)² / δ², where δ is the minimum detectable effect (MDE), σ² is outcome variance, z_α is the critical value for your false-positive rate (typically 0.05), and z_β for power (typically 0.80). Undersized experiments produce noisy results; oversized ones waste time.

3. RANDOMISATION & ASSIGNMENT — Use a deterministic hash (e.g. SHA-256(entity_id + experiment_id) mod 100) so assignment is stable across sessions but unpredictable. Stratified or blocked randomisation on key covariates (industry, firmographic segment, historical spend tier) reduces variance without bias.

4. GUARDRAIL & PRIMARY METRICS — Choose ONE primary metric (e.g. pipeline conversion rate) and several guardrail metrics (e.g. data quality score, churn rate) that must not degrade. Testing multiple primary metrics inflates Type I error — use Bonferroni or Benjamini-Hochberg correction if unavoidable.

5. CUPED (Controlled-experiment Using Pre-Experiment Data) — A powerful variance reduction technique. Regress the outcome Y on a pre-experiment covariate X (same metric measured before the experiment): Y_cuped = Y - θ(X - E[X]), where θ = Cov(Y,X)/Var(X). This can cut required sample sizes by 30–70% with zero bias cost.

6. SEQUENTIAL TESTING & EARLY STOPPING — Classical fixed-horizon tests are invalidated by peeking. Sequential tests (e.g. always-valid p-values using e-values, or alpha-spending functions like O'Brien-Fleming) let you monitor continuously and stop early for efficacy or futility without inflating false-positive rates.

7. STATISTICAL INFERENCE — Compute the test statistic, confidence interval, and p-value. For conversion metrics use a z-test on proportions; for revenue or continuous metrics use Welch's t-test or bootstrap CIs if distributions are heavy-tailed. Report effect size with CI, not just p-value significance.

8. SHIP/NO-SHIP DECISION — Combine statistical significance with practical significance (is δ large enough to matter commercially?) and guardrail status. Log everything to an experiment registry (e.g. integrated with MLflow or a dedicated platform like Statsig, Eppo, or GrowthBook).
data_science.when_to_use: Use A/B testing whenever you need causal evidence rather than correlation — launching a new predictive model score into a sales workflow (does it actually lift pipeline?), testing email personalisation driven by intent signals, validating a new territory carving algorithm, or comparing two entity resolution strategies on match precision. Do NOT use it when: (a) you cannot randomise (e.g. one market, one product launch), use difference-in-differences or synthetic control instead; (b) the effect takes years to materialise; (c) ethical constraints prevent withholding a clearly superior treatment. Prefer multi-armed bandits over pure A/B when you want to minimise regret (route traffic to the winner dynamically) — useful for real-time model serving decisions.
data_science.worked_example:
SCENARIO — D&B's Prospecting Agent surfaces a ranked list of target accounts to an inside sales rep each morning. The data science team has trained a new Buydex-enhanced propensity model (v2) and wants to know if it actually increases qualified meetings booked versus the current Paydex-only model (v1).

STEP 1 — Unit: Randomise at the DUNS entity level (not rep level) to avoid rep-level behavioural confounding. Stratify by industry vertical and company size decile.

STEP 2 — Metrics: Primary = qualified meetings booked per account surfaced (7-day window). Guardrails = data quality complaint rate, rep satisfaction score, pipeline attribution accuracy.

STEP 3 — Sample size: Historical conversion rate = 4.2%. MDE = 0.6pp (a meaningful lift). At α=0.05, power=0.80: n ≈ 17,400 accounts per arm. With ~40K accounts active in the prospecting pool, a two-week run is sufficient.

STEP 4 — CUPED: Use each account's trailing 90-day meeting booking rate as the pre-experiment covariate. This reduces variance by ~45%, cutting the required run time nearly in half.

STEP 5 — Sequential monitoring: Use an O'Brien-Fleming alpha-spending function so the team can check results weekly without p-hacking. Set a futility boundary at week 1 — if the observed effect is less than 20% of MDE, stop early and avoid wasting rep time.

STEP 6 — Result: After 10 days, v2 shows +0.8pp lift (CI: [0.3pp, 1.3pp], p=0.003). Guardrails all green. Ship decision: roll v2 to 100% of the prospecting pool.

STEP 7 — Log to experiment registry with full lineage: model version, feature set, assignment hash seed, CUPED covariate, result, and ship rationale. This becomes ground-truth evidence for the next model iteration and for explaining to sales leadership why the AI recommendation changed.
